correctness.rationale: The characteristic-three translation identity makes e4 on e1=0 descend along the diagonal vector, hence gives the claimed projective cone. In the section x6=0, equality of the six derivatives reduces to xi³+e2 xi=0; Euler's identity applies since degree four is invertible. A nonzero solution has e2≠0, so its coordinates lie in {0,r,−r}. The e1 and e2 identities force either two opposite nonzero entries or a pattern with five nonzero entries of multiplicities 4 and 1, the latter becoming a pair difference after translation. This exhausts the geometric singular points of the section. The two orbit representatives give nondegenerate quadratic terms of Hessian determinants 1 and 1. Isolated nodes imply reducedness and irreducibility here (two surface components in P³ would intersect in positive dimension); the hypersurface is normal by Serre's criterion. Adjunction, H¹(O)=0 and the rational crepant resolution give K3, and the 15 orthogonal exceptional curves and positive-square hyperplane class give the Picard bound. The local product away from the cone vertex gives the transverse type and the quartic equation gives multiplicity four at the vertex. Independent F3 enumeration confirmed 25 and 76 total points, 15 and 46 singular rational points, and the claimed lines; the affine-line fibers prove the all-extension count relation.
residual_risks: The finite check is over F3 only; geometric completeness uses the derivative and root argument. No scheme-theoretic Jacobian decomposition, exact Picard rank or zeta polynomial is asserted.
